parakeet: What's up, everybody, and welcome back to my channel. For this one, I would like to invite you all to sit in somewhat from a peripheral as I share a message to pastors who may find themselves in the closet of non-belief. I share this message with you, not as a critic, but as someone who deeply understands, appreciates, and respects your dedication to the pastoral assignment. You've spent years, perhaps decades, even nurturing, guiding, and cultivating your church community through life's many experiences, trials, and testimonies. Your compassion and commitment have been evident in every message, every prayer, and every act of kindness that you've demonstrated. Yet I know that many of you may be struggling with a profound and very private challenge, and that is your own non-belief. As you may know, I can very well identify with the weight of this internal conflict. The very foundations upon which you have built your life's work, your legacy, and so it may very well feel shaky for you right now, even terrifying. And the questions that once had clear answers now seem unsettingly, unsettlingly complex, or even worse, unsettlingly clear. This struggle does not diminish your value or even your self-assigned purpose. Because as the fog clears, you'll soon realize that you chose this path for a reason. If anything, it enhances your capacity for empathy and understanding if you allow it to. It places you in a unique position to connect with those who are grappling with doubt and seeking to find meaning in the madness of misinformation. And I urge you, as a former brother in the faith, to not hide behind what is expected of you because it is comfortable. Instead, step out and do what is desperately needed. People need your honesty, your uncertainty, and your willingness to update your understanding and message with accurate and helpful information. You may no longer have your faith, but your passion for helping others remains undiminished. The desire to make a positive impact in your community is likely as strong as ever. This passion, backed by your experience and commitment to people, is your greatest asset. It transcends any belief and taps into the very essence of what it means to be human, to care for one another, to lift each other up, and to create spaces where people feel safe and valued, where they can safely explore their own questions without fear of judgment or condemnation. I'm not necessarily telling you to walk away from the pulpit. If you fill that tug, do what you need to do. Instead, I'm asking you to imagine what your church could become if you could help it embrace a new direction. One that is progressive thinking, people centric, and life affirming affirming, life celebrating, even. You have the ability to foster an environment where honest dialogue is encouraged, where questions are welcomed and where every individual is seen as inherently valuable. Your messages can become conversations that inspire hope and action, discovering with your community new ways to focus on love, compassion, and people rather than deities, doctrine, and dogma. You may be in the greatest position to start breaking some of the shackles that have bound religious communities for far too long. By openly addressing such issues as equality, justice, and the importance of critical thinking, you can lead your church, your congregation, your community into a new era of enlightenment and acceptance. This is not about abandoning your sense of calling, but about enriching it with a deeper understanding of humanity and the wonderful world that we live in. Many of your churches can become safe havens for people. Period. Places where everyone, regardless of their background, beliefs, or doubts, feels welcomed and supported without the need for conformity or uniformity. By fostering inclusivity and understanding, you can create a community that truly reflects the teachings of love and compassion that we so desperately want it to believe was at the heart of many religious traditions. You can use your voice to help guide people back from the brink of divinely imposed brokenness and help them uncover the boundless capacity of human agency and the power of community. We live in a world that is still learning how to pull itself together. We face countless challenges from social injustice to environmental crises, and we desperately need leaders like you to help cultivate communities that can rise to meet these challenges. Your passion can drive initiatives that bring people together, promote cooperation, understanding, and collective action beyond the bounds of outdated and harmful superstitions. You are in a powerful position to make a difference. Your journey may be complex, and the road ahead will likely be challenging. But your potential, your capacity to effect positive change is immense. Embrace this opportunity to lead with compassion and honesty and to create a legacy that is both transformative and enduring. If this message finds a home in your mind, please reach out, and I will do everything within my capacity to help you start making the transition, regardless of where you are in your journey, without causing any undue harm. And my commitment to you is that if you reach out to me, it will remain confidential until you're ready for it to be otherwise. I love you, and I hope I caught you in time. Until next time, keep rising.
